items.t: Garrison Crossing is a 153-acre redevelopment on former Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Chilliwack land in the City of Chilliwack, and that former-base origin is the boundary fact that defines the neighbourhood.
Canada Lands Company acquired the property, formerly part of CFB Chilliwack, from the federal government in 2011, and developed it in cooperation with the City of Chilliwack.
The neighbourhood's central boulevard links to a network of bikeways, pathways and nature trails, and to the retail centre called Garrison Village.
The City's Sardis-Vedder parks list places Garrison-named parks inside this area's park set, including All Sappers Memorial Park, Chehalis Park, Mitchell Gardens and the Garrison Woodlot nature park.
The Sardis Neighbourhood Plan treats Garrison Crossing as the area to the south of Sardis, connected along the Vedder Corridor, rather than as part of the Sardis neighbourhood itself.

The stock is a deliberate mix of refurbished base housing and new housing: Garrison Crossing includes more than 1,700 residential housing units, comprising refurbished single-family homes, new and restored townhouses and condominium apartments.
Permanent Married Quarters (PMQs) that originally existed on the site were refurbished, with care taken to preserve the residences' original fir floors.
The community was modelled on the principles of new urbanism and was intentionally designed to be pedestrian-friendly and to encourage travel without a vehicle.

blocks.text: Garrison Crossing: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Heritage on this site is a design fact a buyer inherits, not a marketing line: Canada Lands preserved elements of the former military base, built the Legacy Walk honouring those who lived and worked at CFB Chilliwack from 1942 to its closure in 1995, and renovated Sappers Cenotaph Park on the eastern edge of the site with local veterans.

Which Official Community Plan (OCP) neighbourhood-plan schedule covers a specific Garrison Crossing lot must be read on the City's OCP page and webmap, because the OCP lists the Sardis plan as Schedule B5 and the South Vedder plan as Schedule B6 as separate schedules.

blocks.text: Garrison Crossing: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Legacy Walk, also called the Legacy Trail, is inside the neighbourhood and is listed in the City's Sardis-Vedder trails list alongside the Vedder Rotary Loop Trail and Peach Creek Rotary Trail.
Sappers Cenotaph Park sits on the eastern edge of the site and was renovated and rededicated in partnership with local veterans.
The City parks list for this area names the Garrison Woodlot as a nature park and Mitchell Gardens, Chehalis Park, Dieppe Park and Cowichan Park among its smaller parks.

The Canada Education Park institutions south of the Vedder River, including the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus, are reached from Garrison Crossing along the Vedder Corridor bus connection described in the Sardis plan.

blocks.text: Garrison Crossing: development and new projects

items.t: Garrison Crossing, former CFB Chilliwack lands, City of Chilliwack, Canada Lands Company, master-planned redevelopment of 153 acres with more than 1,700 residential units (refurbished single-family homes, new and restored townhouses, condominium apartments) and the Garrison Village retail centre — STATUS: completed, described by Canada Lands as a now-completed development, read 2026-11-03.

The tenure check specific to this area is lot by lot: the stock mixes refurbished former PMQ houses with new strata townhouses and condominium apartments, so a buyer should confirm from title whether the specific home is freehold or strata before comparing carrying costs.

Walking and cycling are the designed first mode inside Garrison Crossing: the central boulevard links to bikeways, pathways and nature trails to the elementary school, community centre and Garrison Village.

The Sardis plan describes a frequent bus line on the Vedder Corridor, stated in the plan as 15-minute service, connecting Sardis to downtown, Garrison Crossing and the Canada Education Park to the south.

Route 51 Vedder, in the BC Transit Chilliwack Rider's Guide, runs the Vedder Road corridor between downtown Chilliwack and the University of the Fraser Valley Chilliwack campus, the corridor a Garrison Crossing rider uses to leave the neighbourhood.
The Vedder Rotary Loop Trail at the south end of the area is listed in the City's Sardis-Vedder trails list.

blocks.text: Garrison Crossing: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the title of a refurbished PMQ carefully: the homes were base housing refurbished in a single redevelopment, so a buyer should have the title, any covenants and the building's renovation permits reviewed rather than treat the house as a conventional resale of its apparent age.

Check which OCP schedule and development permit areas apply to the specific lot on the City's OCP page and webmap, because the OCP's Schedule D permit areas include drinking water, hillside, riparian and residential form-and-character areas that apply differently by location.

faq.a: Yes, the housing area was part of Canadian Forces Base Chilliwack. Canada Lands states it acquired the property from the federal government in 2011, refurbished Permanent Married Quarters already on the site, and built the Legacy Walk to honour the men and women who lived and worked at the base from its inception in 1942 to its closure in 1995.
faq.q: Was this really a military base?

faq.a: Canada Lands describes Garrison Crossing as a now-completed development. Its own project page states the completed community includes more than 1,700 residential units in refurbished single-family homes, new and restored townhouses and condominium apartments, plus the Garrison Village retail centre, so a buyer here is buying resale housing in a completed master plan rather than a future phase.

The community was designed so residents can walk to the local elementary school, community centre and Garrison Village by the central boulevard, bikeways, pathways and nature trails, per Canada Lands. 33 (SD33), so confirm the exact address in the SD33 School Locator rather than relying on walking distance alone.
faq.q: Can children walk to school inside the neighbourhood?

faq.a: The difference is the single master plan. Sardis grew street by street under the Sardis Neighbourhood Plan, while Garrison Crossing was one 153-acre redevelopment that kept refurbished base houses, added townhouses and apartments, and centred the area on a boulevard and the Garrison Village retail centre, all under new urbanism principles stated by Canada Lands.
faq.q: How is this different from the Sardis streets next door?
